query: Which MS acquisition mode (DIA vs DDA) and fragment-scoring pipeline gives optimal sensitivity and specificity for site-level protease cleavage calls in peptide libraries?

response.query: Which MS acquisition mode (DIA vs DDA) and fragment-scoring pipeline gives optimal sensitivity and specificity for site-level protease cleavage calls in peptide libraries?
response.answer: DIA acquisition mode combined with Fragpipe-MSFragger scoring pipeline offers optimal sensitivity and specificity for site-level protease cleavage calls in peptide libraries. MSFragger-DDA+ also shows strong performance for DDA data.

results.title: MSFragger-DDA+ enhances peptide identification ...
results.content: Here, we introduce MSFragger-DDA+, a database search algorithm that enhances peptide identification by detecting co-fragmented peptides with high sensitivity and speed. The above datasets from two laboratories with different sample preparation and data acquisition configurations demonstrate that MSFragger-DDA+ performs well for identifying peptides from WWA data. Unlike conventional tools developed for DDA data, it starts by searching MS2 spectra against all peptides within the full isolation window to enable identification of all possible co-fragmentated ions. In the original MSFragger11.") manuscript we demonstrated the application of fragment ion indexing to open (also known as mass tolerant or unrestricted) searches of DDA data to identify modified peptides. With MSFragger-DDA+, we now return to the analysis of conventional DDA data and enable the identification of co-fragmented peptides from chimeric DDA spectra using full isolation window search. To summarize, with the spectrum-centric database search framework at its core, the MSFragger family of tools unifies peptide identification across different MS2 data acquisition modalities (DDA, wide window DDA, DIA) and different search modes (closed, open, and mass-offset).
